children.text: From actual database design and `org.routes.js` — 51 KB:
Every institution is a row in the `organizations` table with a unique `org_id`. All other tables (`attendance_sessions`, `student_fees`, `library_books`, `assignments`, etc.) have an `org_id` column.

Every database query from API routes includes `.eq('org_id', orgId)`. This is enforced at the application layer on every single route. A faculty at College A cannot access assignment data from College B even if they know the ID.

The `isAuthenticated` middleware extracts `organization_id` from the authenticated user's JWT and attaches it as `req.effectiveOrganizationId`. Every route handler uses this value — never trusting user-supplied org IDs.
Each organization deployed at its own subdomain: `campusname.classgrid.com`. The public-facing website, API endpoints, and Razorpay keys are all scoped to this subdomain.

Each organization stores its own `razorpay_key_id` and `razorpay_key_secret` in the org configuration. The fee payment flow fetches the organization's own keys, not a platform-wide key. This means all student payments go directly into the institution's Razorpay account — not Classgrid's.
